common_name: Thickleaf Wild Petunia (Smooth Wild Petunia, South Florida Native)

planting.note: Set divisions or nursery transplants into sharply drained, sandy or limerock-derived soil once soil has warmed after the last frost; this pine rockland native resents heavy, wet clay.

directions: Thickleaf wild petunia is a diminutive South Florida endemic valued by native-plant gardeners for its fleshy, succulent foliage and lavender-purple blooms produced through the warm months. Site it in sharply drained, low-fertility sandy or limestone-derived soil that mimics the pine rockland and mesic flatwoods habitat where it naturally occurs, and avoid coastal salt spray, which it does not tolerate. Once established it handles dry spells well and needs little supplemental watering or feeding. Because it hosts common buckeye and malachite butterfly larvae, it is a worthwhile addition to a South Florida butterfly garden; source plants or divisions from a native-plant nursery rather than collecting from wild populations, which are limited to a handful of counties.
sources: Florida Native Plant Society (FNPS) Plant Profiles
